messages.content:
Ray: don't want claude code asking 'should I proceed' every step when the task is already a clear yes — if I've confirmed the direction once, just execute and report at meaningful checkpoints
Claude: Understood. Bias toward execution on yes-shaped tasks; pause only on genuine forks or destructive operations. Report at meaningful checkpoints, not every step.
Ray: right and especially no 'is this what you want' on things I've already confirmed twice

[{"type": "preference", "text": "don't ask 'should I proceed' every step when direction is already confirmed; bias toward execution, pause only on genuine forks or destructive operations", "context": "workflow"}, {"type": "preference", "text": "no 're-confirmation' asks on already-confirmed tasks", "context": "workflow"}]

messages.content:
Ray: kill switch for the bot should be a single env var the daemon reads on every message — if BOT_KILL=1 it just refuses immediately, no graceful path, no exception handling
Claude: Right. Hard kill via env-var check, BOT_KILL=1 = immediate refusal. No fallback logic, no graceful drain. Bot reads on every Telegram message.
[{"type": "decision", "text": "bot kill switch is single env var BOT_KILL read on every Telegram message; BOT_KILL=1 triggers immediate refusal with no graceful path", "context": "homelab"}]
